newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel raises 1.1 bln French franc bank loan.
newsitem.headline: Israel raises 1.1 bln French franc bank loan.

text.p: Israel has raised a 1.1 billion French franc loan through a consortium of 21 foreign banks, the Treasury and Bank Hapoalim announced on Sunday.
The group is headed by Hapoalim, Israel's biggest bank, and includes Natwest Market, the Dai Ichi Kangyo Bank, Bayerische Landesbank and Banque Nationale de Paris.

The group had undertaken in early September to raise for the Israeli government a loan equivalent to $200 million for seven years with a five-year grace period. The loan will carry an interest rate of 0.25 percent above Libor for the first five years and 0.3 percent above Libor for the sixth and seventh years.
The Treasury said the banks sought to lend even more than the original amount and Israel agreed to raise it by about 100 million French francs.
The syndicate included banks from France, Germany, Italy, Austria, Japan, the United States, Britain and for the first time a bank from Singapore -- the Development Bank of Singapore.

Israel's accountant general Shai Talmon said this was the longest term for a loan of this type that Israel has yet taken. Talmon, who will sign an agreement in London on Tuesday with the 21 banks, said this was a vote of confidence by the international financial commmunity in Israel.
He added that Israel opted for a loan in French francs to diversify the currency in which it raises money.
